original_value: The delay-and-sum imaging algorithm is a promising crack localization approach for crack detection and monitoring of key structural regions. Most studies successfully offer a hole-like damage position. However, cracks are more common than hole-like damages in a structure. To solve this issue, this paper presents a crack localization approach, based on diffraction wave theory, which is capable of imaging crack endpoints. The guided wave propagated to the crack endpoints and transformed into a diffraction wave. A line sensor array was used to record the diffraction waveform. Then, dispersion compensation was applied to shorten the dispersive wave packets and separate the overlapping wave packets. Subsequently, half-wave compensation was executed to improve the localization accuracy. Finally, the effectiveness of this high-resolution crack localization method was validated by an experimental example.

result.paraphrase: The delay-and-sum imaging algorithm is a promising method for localizing cracks in the detection and monitoring of key structural regions. Although most studies can successfully indicate hole-like damage locations, cracks are more common than hole-like damage in structures. To address this problem, this paper proposes a crack localization approach based on diffraction wave theory that can image crack endpoints. Guided waves propagate to the crack endpoints and are converted into diffraction waves. A line sensor array records the diffraction waveform. Dispersion compensation is then applied to shorten dispersive wave packets and separate overlapping ones. Next, half-wave compensation is carried out to improve localization accuracy. Finally, an experimental example validates the effectiveness of this high-resolution crack localization method.
